text:
jon: Heads up — we're seeing exporter stalls to telemetry-prod (OTLP endpoint) when the backend starts returning 5xx. Process ends up stuck on shutdown; SDK stop() doesn't always flush while gRPC stream is stuck. Anyone run into this?

maya: Yep. We've seen similar. Two practical levers: per-exporter RPC deadlines + dial/connect timeouts, and a quick fallback to HTTP/protobuf if grpc dial fails. Also limit queue depth so shutdown can drain predictably.

phil: Agree on queue limits. Also add a circuit breaker on repeated failures so we stop piling on retries into a blocked stream. Example config we used in staging (otel-collector side):
```yaml
exporters:
  otlp/grpc:
    endpoint: telemetry-prod.redwood:4317
    timeout: 5s # per-RPC deadline
    retry_on: UNAVAILABLE,RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED
    backoff:
      initial_interval: 200ms
      max_interval: 8s
      max_elapsed_time: 30s
    headers:
      x-rw-team: platform
```
And in SDK: small batching + flush interval 2s, max_queue_size 500.

kevin: Important: dedupe/at-least-once semantics. If we aggressively retry during shutdown we can double-send spans. HTTP supports idempotency header patterns (we surfaced `x-rw-idempotency-key`). OTLP/gRPC doesn't standardize that — we can add a per-process incremental export-id and let backends ignore duplicates by id.

lina: Proposal for default behavior in console + SDK:
- prefer: grpc
- fallback: http/protobuf if grpc dial doesn't succeed within 500ms
- per-exporter deadline: 5s
- retry budget: 10 attempts/min with exponential backoff + full jitter (cap 8s)
- queue: max 1000 spans per exporter; on SIGTERM start draining and stop accepting new spans, give drain_timeout=20s then force flush/drop
- circuit-breaker: open after 5 consecutive RPC failures for 30s
Any objections?

jon: No objections. Couple of notes: need an integration test that simulates a backend that accepts connection but then returns intermittent UNAVAILABLE and that also delays stream close — to exercise drain logic. Also make sure metrics expose "exporter_queue_drops" so teams can see when we hit queue caps.

phil: We should also ensure our agent/process uses keepalive settings for gRPC (to detect dead peers faster) and tune TCP timeouts on dedicated instances.

kevin: On the idempotency plan: I'll draft a small RFC for adding export-id on the Resource/Batch level — makes dedupe easier for backends.

deploy-bot: deploy:telemetry-exporter-config v1.7 -> canary started (platform infra) :rocket:

jon: I'll open the SDK PR with the shutdown hooks + config defaults. Putting the collector exporter config in the canary too. Will add the integration test cases.

lina: Thanks — if we can get the canary metrics in 12h we can decide whether to roll to prod. :thumbsup:
